landing.story.hero.body: Your services in one place, your institution’s infrastructure in one cloud.
landing.story.hero.eyebrow: A QUIET MOMENT BEFORE WHAT'S NEXT
landing.story.hero.footerTagline: Where the light lingers, and what's next begins.
landing.story.server.label: Cloud servers
landing.story.server.title: The server you need. Ready for research.
landing.story.server.body: Choose compute, memory and storage to prepare your research server.
landing.story.server.graphic: Concept diagram connecting compute, storage and networking to a project’s research virtual server
landing.story.gpu.label: GPU AI training
landing.story.gpu.title: From data to your next model.
landing.story.gpu.body: Connect your data and research environment to a GPU server to start training a model.
landing.story.gpu.graphic: Concept diagram showing data flowing through GPU compute to a trained model
landing.story.gateway.label: LLM gateway
landing.story.gateway.title: Many models. One connection.
landing.story.gateway.body: Lumen brings multiple AI providers behind one gateway. Each researcher gets an API key and connects coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex directly.
landing.story.gateway.graphic: Concept diagram showing providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini connected through the Lumen gateway to researchers' Claude Code and Codex
landing.story.mcp.label: MCP connection
landing.story.mcp.title: Agents look after the cloud themselves.
landing.story.mcp.body: Connect Afterglow as an MCP server and coding agents can inspect VMs, volumes, networks and quotas, and run management actions such as start and stop within the permissions you grant.
landing.story.mcp.graphic: Concept diagram showing a coding agent using Afterglow MCP tools to check VM status in the research cloud and restart a stopped VM
landing.story.mcp.prompt: Check the GPU VMs and restart any that stopped
landing.story.kubernetes.label: Kubernetes
landing.story.kubernetes.title: Containers come together. Research services take shape.
landing.story.kubernetes.body: Combine nodes into a cluster to run container-based services.
landing.story.kubernetes.graphic: Concept diagram showing containers distributed across nodes in one Kubernetes cluster
landing.story.onprem.label: Institutional cloud deployment
landing.story.onprem.title: Your infrastructure. Your institution’s cloud.
landing.story.onprem.body: We bring servers, GPUs, storage and networking together into an internal cloud shared by research teams.
landing.story.onprem.graphic: Concept diagram showing institutional servers, GPUs, storage and networking combined into one cloud for research team projects
landing.story.motion.example: A concept diagram of how the service works, not actual resources or progress.
landing.story.availability: Available resources, AI models and access depend on institutional configuration and policy.

claudeConsent.error.checkCode: Check the 8-character connection code shown in Claude Code.
claudeConsent.error.invalidUrlCode: The Claude Code authentication code in the connection URL is invalid. You can enter the code manually.

claudeConsent.approved.title: Claude Code connection approved.

claudeConsent.denied.title: Claude Code connection denied.
claudeConsent.denied.body: No Lumen API key will be issued for this authentication request.
claudeConsent.error.title: Unable to process the connection request.
claudeConsent.details.scopeDescription: Model listing and Claude Code inference
claudeConsent.code.label: Claude Code connection code
claudeConsent.warning.title: Only approve requests you initiated.
claudeConsent.warning.body: Approving issues a Lumen credential only once, valid for 24 hours and tied to the current user and project. Your password and existing API keys are not shared with Claude Code.
mcpConsent.error.loadFailed: Couldn't load the OAuth approval request.
mcpConsent.error.durationUnconfirmed: The server did not confirm the requested authorization duration. Approval may already be recorded; do not retry here. Check the connection under Account → MCP, remove it if needed, then reconnect.
mcpConsent.error.invalidRequest: The OAuth approval request is invalid.
mcpConsent.error.missingOrExpired: The OAuth approval request is missing or has expired.
mcpConsent.title: Approve external AI access
mcpConsent.description: Check the external client, then choose the access level and projects to allow. Defaults are read-only access and the current project.
mcpConsent.error.title: Unable to process the approval request.
mcpConsent.duration.title: Authorization duration
mcpConsent.duration.help: Approving with this option lets the client renew short-lived access tokens without another sign-in. The approved projects, scopes and role ceilings never expand, and current access is rechecked.
mcpConsent.duration.untilRevoked: Active until you revoke it — automatic renewal applies instead of the finite expiration shown earlier.
mcpConsent.duration.finite: Expires {deadline} — reconnect and approve again afterward.
mcpConsent.duration.defaultHelp: Authorization continues until you revoke it by default. Turn off automatic renewal in the next step to use the expiration above instead.
mcpConsent.duration.revocation: Remove this connection under Account → MCP to stop access for every client sharing it. Existing finite approvals are not extended automatically; reconnect and approve once to continue using them.
mcpConsent.duration.unsupported: This server has not confirmed automatic renewal support. Only finite authorization until the displayed expiration is available.
mcpConsent.manage.title: Manage access to approve
mcpConsent.manage.body: Changes are limited to each project's current permissions. All projects does not give write access to read-only projects. Review each project's result below before approving.
mcpConsent.read.title: Read access to approve
mcpConsent.read.body: This client can only use safe read-only tools in the approved projects.
mcpConsent.access.label: Access level
mcpConsent.access.help: You can narrow a manage request to read-only access.
mcpConsent.access.manageUnavailable: Manage is unavailable because the client did not request it.
mcpConsent.projects.label: Project scope
mcpConsent.projects.help: All projects is a snapshot at approval time; projects added later are not included.
mcpConsent.projects.empty: Select at least one project to approve.
mcpConsent.preview.title: Project permissions after approval
mcpConsent.preview.help: Project cloud permissions and the access selected for this key or approval are separate. Read-only access never grants writes. Service permissions are confirmed independently and limited by the selected access level; they are not a list of MCP tools. Only supported tools can run, and current permissions are checked again at execution. This preview alone grants no access.
mcpClients.count: {count, plural, one {# observed client signature} other {# observed client signatures}}
mcpConsent.preview.loading: Checking project and service permissions… Read-only creation remains available.
mcpConsent.preview.unavailable: Permission preview is unavailable. Unknown permissions are not confirmed access. Read-only creation remains available; refresh to check again.
mcpConsent.preview.service.attenuated: No permissions allowed by read-only consent
mcpConsent.preview.scopeUnavailable: The project's authentication scope could not be verified, so service policies were not checked. This does not establish that access is denied.
mcpConsent.preview.unknownWrite: Write permission could not be verified for a project. Manage approval is unavailable. Choose read only or reopen the request.
mcpConsent.preview.selectedReadOnly: Your selection includes a read-only project, so manage approval is unavailable. Choose read only, or deselect the read-only projects.
